bull.b: Higher gross margin and five consecutive quarters of positive adjusted EBITDA indicate improving operating leverage and a more favorable revenue mix. If sustained, this transition toward software, services, and edge hardware can strengthen earnings quality and reduce reliance on lower-margin resale activity.

Growth in software revenue and recurring ARR supports a more durable business model because subscription and platform activity can compound as managed assets and customer relationships expand. This mix also offers greater predictability and margin potential than project-based or resale revenue.

Expansion across multiple countries and utility-scale projects broadens Stem’s commercial footprint and demonstrates demand beyond a single market. Larger deployments can increase the assets managed by its platform, supporting future software adoption, recurring revenue, and competitive relevance.

bear.b: Sustained negative equity and debt exceeding the asset base materially reduce financial flexibility. This can constrain investment, increase refinancing pressure, and make future capital needs more likely to be addressed through equity issuance or other actions that may dilute existing holders.

The sharp decline in battery resale revenue and reliance on second-half timing make near-term revenue conversion less predictable. Hardware resale can also dilute the mix and pressure margins, weakening confidence that reported growth will consistently reflect durable software and services expansion.

Although operating cash flow has improved, negative trailing free cash flow shows the business is not yet consistently self-funding after investment. The history of large cash deficits from 2021 through 2024 increases execution risk and may require additional financing if improvement fades.
